subject: AWS Marketplace SaaS fulfillment: implementation playlist & test plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <asha@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace SaaS fulfillment: implementation playlist & test plan

Hi Asha / Ravi,

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a concise implementation "playlist" for the AWS Marketplace SaaS fulfillment path so your engineering team can map tasks to owners. This thread will be our single source of truth for integration checkpoints.

High-level goals:
- Enable entitlement provisioning from AWS Marketplace (SaaS-Contract + Entitlements API)
- Ensure usage metering stream to AWS for billing accuracy (sample payloads attached)
- Validate trial -> paid conversion and SSO flows

Suggested milestones (rough order):
1) Contract & entitlement fields finalized (procurement/Rev).
2) Mapping file: Acme plan SKUs -> Redwood product_id (attached entitlement_mapping_v1.csv).
3) Sandbox fulfillment test: POST sample payloads to Redwood test endpoints (S3 link in related_links).
4) Metering verification run with AWS test account (coordinate with AWS contact).
5) Go/no-go cutover checklist + smoke tests.

Action items for this week:
- Asha: confirm final SKU names that must appear on the AWS contract by EOD Thu.
- Ravi: share one sample subscriber record and desired entitlement fields.
- Marissa: I think you can own mapping validation and a small runbook for troubleshooting.

Attachments: redwood_saas_fulfillment_checklist.xlsx; entitlement_mapping_v1.csv

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>

Date: 2027-04-04T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace SaaS fulfillment: implementation playlist & test plan

Hi Diego / Asha,

Thanks for the clear checklist. A couple of quick notes from the AWS side:
1) For SaaS subscriptions we recommend including both the Marketplace SKU and the SellerDefinedProductId in the entitlement payload to avoid ambiguity during reconciliation.
2) Metering: send UsageRecords with a consistent usageDimensionName; if you expect bursty traffic, include a reasonable Timestamp and Quantity to avoid duplication on reconciliation.
3) We'll need a test integration environment (sandbox account) — please provide the account id you will use so we can whitelist endpoints for the metering verification.

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute run-through next week with our Marketplace Tech Enablement engineer.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Support
AWS Marketplace Team

[Attachment: aws_saa_sbx_instructions.txt (TXT)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Asha Patel <asha@acme-analytics.com>, AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace SaaS fulfillment: implementation playlist & test plan

Thanks — looping in a slightly more tactical checklist and what we'll test during the sandbox window. I've attached an implementation checklist spreadsheet with tasks and expected outputs. Below are the run steps I propose for the sandbox verification window:

Sandbox verification run (owner in parentheses):
- Upload entitlement_mapping_v1.csv to our test runner and validate that each SKU resolves to a Redwood product_id and price_tier. (Marissa)
- Provision 3 test subscribers via the AWS Entitlements API (Asha/Ravi)
- Send 10 usage samples to the Redwood metering intake endpoint (POST /marketplace/usage) using the sample payloads in S3. Monitor for duplicate suppression and correct aggregation. (Karthik)
- Verify that the UsageRecords produced in Redwood reconcile to the expected quantities that AWS reports. (Marissa/Karthik)
- Run contract to subscription flow: ensure trial subscriber created in Redwood shows expected entitlements and that conversion/downgrade events map to SKU changes. (Diego/Ravi)

Notes and gotchas:
- Keep SKU string length under 60 characters to avoid truncation in older AWS flows.
- If your contract uses custom attributes (e.g., team_size), include them in the SellerDefinedAttributes JSON field so we can persist them in our tenant metadata.

DocuSign link for the final SaaS Marketplace addendum: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/sign/DOC-ACME-2027 (Asha, please countersign once procurement confirms SKUs).

Attachments: redwood_saas_fulfillment_checklist.xlsx

—
Marissa Cole
Marketplace Integrations | Redwood Inference
